title: SWL course
abstract: Getting started in amateur radio as a short-wave listener: receiving equipment, radio operation, QSL cards and preparation for the DARC's DE examination.

chapters.title: Getting started in amateur radio reception
chapters.abstract: We get to know the hobby of short-wave listeners, distinguish listening from transmitting and put together a first receiving station.

chapters.title: Receivers in detail: types of modulation and connectors
chapters.abstract: We operate a receiver, choose the right mode and recognise the common RF connectors.

chapters.title: Propagation
chapters.abstract: The ionosphere makes worldwide short-wave reception possible; special conditions open up long distances on higher frequencies too.

chapters.title: Safety
chapters.abstract: Even a receive-only station needs a safe power supply and a properly erected antenna installation.

chapters.title: Call signs, countries and bands
chapters.abstract: We read amateur radio call signs, identify important country prefixes and link frequency ranges with the usual band names.

chapters.title: Language on the bands
chapters.abstract: The phonetic alphabet, operating abbreviations and Q codes help you to understand radio contacts reliably, even weak ones or ones in a foreign language.

chapters.title: Listening in practice
chapters.abstract: We assess signals, follow special operating situations and record the radio contacts we hear in the log and on SWL QSL cards.

chapters.title: Legal aspects
chapters.abstract: Listening is in principle unrestricted, but the prohibition of interception and the duty of confidentiality set clear limits. We also distinguish between the listening amateur, the radio amateur and the amateur station.

chapters.title: DE examination and DE identifier
chapters.abstract: We look at the procedure and content of the DE examination, the system of DE identifiers and the way from the application to the certificate.

chapters.title: Awards and next goals
chapters.abstract: Confirmed listener reports open the way to the DLD-SWL (Germany Award for SWLs), to the Deutscher Empfangsmeister (German Reception Master) and perhaps later to your own amateur radio certificate.
